text: OVERDOSE Iron: Signs and Symptoms: Iron is toxic. Acute overdosage of iron may cause nausea and vomiting. In severe cases, iron overdose can cause cardiovascular collapse and death. Other symptoms include pallor and cyanosis, melena, shock, drowsiness and coma. The estimated overdose of orally ingested iron is 300mg/kg body weight. When overdoses are ingested by children, severe reactions, including fatalities have resulted. Multi-Nate DHA Extra 295/430 mg should be stored beyond the reach of children to prevent against accidental iron poisoning. Keep this and all other drugs out of reach of children. Treatment: For specific therapy, exchange transfusion and chelating agents should be used. For general management, perform gastric lavage with sodium bicarbonate solution or milk. Administer intravenous fluids and electrolytes and use oxygen.
